title: add-frequency-domain-residuals-detector-and-graceful-threshold-adapter
author: Miguel Torres
description: Motivation: transient, periodic interference (GC sweeps, noisy neighbors, periodic telemetry jobs) has caused low-amplitude latency regressions that percentile-only detectors occasionally miss and that can trigger noisy rollbacks. This PR introduces a new detector that analyzes latency time-series in the frequency domain and fuses spectral residual signals with existing percentile drift metrics to produce a more stable canary signal. Design summary: 1) Windowed FFT transform of per-request p95/p99 time series over short sliding windows (configurable); 2) Compute spectral residual energy in targeted bands (e.g., 0.5-5s cycles) and normalize by traffic power to be traffic-aware; 3) Produce a residuals_score time series and combine with percentile delta via a probabilistic fusion step (logistic weight based on signal SNR); 4) Graceful Threshold Adapter: thresholds are scaled by a lightweight traffic intensity estimator and by recent variance to avoid over-reacting to cold-start or low-sample windows; 5) Rollout guard: when residuals_score exceeds adaptive threshold for N consecutive windows we pause canary traffic and open an investigation alert with suggested probes. Implementation notes: detector implemented in perf-canary/src/detectors/freq_residuals.py using numpy/scipy primitives with a fallback optimized CFFI path for high-throughput hosts; fusion and threshold adapter live in perf-canary/src/eval/fusion.py; added PromQL metric exporters and Grafana panel JSON for visibility under observability/canaries/freq-residuals-panel.json. Tests and validation: unit tests cover spectral normalization, SNR-based weighting, and adapter scaling (perf-canary/tests/test_freq_residuals.py); integration canary harness added to perf-canary/integration/canary-sim that replays synthetic traffic with injected periodic noise to validate true/false-positive curves; load impact: CPU microbenchmarks show ~2% extra CPU on probe workers, latency overhead negligible. Rollout plan: feature flag behind perf.canary.freq_residuals.enabled; start with passive mode (score logged but not gating) for 48h in perf environment, promote to active gating on a small percentage of canaries, then global default after two weeks if false-positive rate < 1% and detection recall improves. Related work: builds on ENG-2480 (spectral baseline) and complements existing percentile-aware detectors in this codebase. Backwards compatibility: detector registers as optional evaluation plugin; default off for existing canaries. Metrics to watch: residuals_score, fused_canary_signal, false_positive_rate, mean_time-to-pause, CPU impact. Operational playbook: added runbook section pointing to runbooks/canaries/freq-residuals-runbook.md with RCA steps and suggested probes. This PR includes code, tests, panels, and runbook entries. Merge notes: squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice approach, could you explain why you chose the 0.5-5s band by default? Also please add a short note about sampling bias when traffic is bursty.
Miguel Torres: Chosen after empirical sweep on 50 canaries; added comment and default rationale to code and docs. Sampling bias mitigation added via traffic power normalization.
Priya Nair: The adaptive thresholding logic looks promising but we should be conservative for low-sample windows. Can we gate adapter aggressiveness behind a minimum sample count?
Miguel Torres: Added a minimum-samples parameter and a unit test; default min_samples=100 to preserve prior behavior.
Liam O'Connor: CI failed on linting for line length in the panel JSON; fixed in last commit. Approved pending CI.
Ava Chen: Approving — observed improved detection on the synthetic harness. Recommend a short training session for SREs on interpreting residuals_score.
CI: All checks passed on re-run (unit, integration, lint, security-scanner)
